main_body: Wooden stall-like piece made of three stacked horizontal wood parts: a top plank/beam (rows 0-4), a middle shelf box holding goods (rows 7-16), and a bottom plank (rows 19-23). Transparent gaps separate them.
top_band: none: the column scan shows only a 1-row lighter line (L=98-131 at row 1) under an outline row. Rows 2-3 are the same tone as the face (L=64), so no top surface is drawn.
evidence: Every part is drawn face-on. The top plank is a flat wood face with a 1px highlight, and the middle box shows barrels or bowls and an orange item straight from the front. The bottom plank is another flat face. In the scan columns x=7, 15 and 22, no band of at least 25 L lighter than the face sits above a front face, and no horizontal surface is visible from above. This matches the guide's red 'front elevation' and 'rim only' cases, so the whole drawing fails.

style.evidence: The measured facts are equal to or better than the references on density: 18 colours per tile against 17 and 20, 0% flat-fill coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is a tinted dark brown. The wood ramp has about 5 steps (#3d220c, #633712, #6f4725, #885a26, #b77541), plus grain dots and an orange/red accent. Total distinct colours (18) are well below the references (38-40), so the palette is narrower. Texture and shading are still comparable to the stall reference and would sit acceptably beside it.
